alternatives.root_cause: A feature flag was flipped in flagd, enabling a failing code path in fraud-detection and the other flag-reading services.
alternatives.why_not: A flag flip changes behavior in the clients, not flagd's own serving latency; the ServiceHighLatency alert on flagd itself points at flagd being unhealthy rather than merely serving a new value.

alternatives.root_cause: flagd's flag-definition store returned unreadable/undecodable content, causing evaluation failures across all clients.
alternatives.why_not: Corrupt flag definitions would produce fast, clean evaluation errors rather than elevated latency on flagd and its callers.

verdict.summary: flagd became slow serving flag-evaluation requests (its own resources — CPU/connection/thread capacity — exhausted), so every service that evaluates flags on the request path (ad, cart, product-reviews, recommendation, fraud-detection) blocked and surfaced errors up through frontend and frontend-proxy to the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is almost exactly the set of flagd clients plus the caller chain above them: fraud-detection, ad/cart/product-reviews/recommendation feed frontend, which feeds frontend-proxy, which feeds load-generator. load-generator alerted first only because it is the outermost caller and sees every failure. flagd itself carries a latency warning, which means it is still answering but slowly — that rules out a freeze or partition (callers would hang with flagd silent) and rules out a pure dependency problem, since flagd is a leaf with no downstream in this graph. A leaf that is up but slow under fan-in load is most often out of some resource (CPU, worker threads, or connection slots). fraud-detection erroring hardest fits a short flag-evaluation deadline being blown.
open_questions: flagd CPU/memory/goroutine and connection counts at onset versus the preceding hour
flagd's own logs: slow evaluation warnings, GC pauses, or accept-queue overflow
whether flagd request volume jumped (client retry storm) or stayed flat while latency rose
whether any flag definition was edited or a new flagd artifact rolled out just before 18:04
fraud-detection error payloads: deadline-exceeded on the flag call versus an application error on a flagged code path
